Internal helper: variable names typed without quotes in vars =

Source: R/recode.R
dot-jst_vars_bare_names.Rd

vars = takes a character vector – the stored or computed list of names, vars = names(d) or vars = myvars – and so R evaluates it: jconvert(d, vars = c(A, B), to = "stata") stopped with R's "object 'A' not found", and a workspace object named A would have been read for its contents (the S351 item). Bare names are the house form after the data frame, and that is where this check sends them (Session 355, ruling R18): when vars = was given a name or a c() of names, and one of them is a variable of the data frame or they do not give a character vector, the call stops with the call rebuilt, the names after the data frame – a workspace object that shares a variable's name is never read. A name the data frame lacks gets the not-found sentence instead. A name holding names (myvars <- c("A", "B")) that is not itself a variable of the data frame is the programmatic form and passes, as does every computed form.

Usage

.jst_vars_bare_names(
  vars_sub,
  env,
  data,
  data_name,
  mc,
  fn,
  dot_names = character(0)
)

Arguments

vars_sub

The vars argument, unevaluated.

env

The caller's environment.

data, data_name

The data frame and its name.

mc

The call, from match.call().

fn

The function's name.

dot_names

Character; variables also given in the dots.

Value

Invisible NULL; stops on bare names.
